dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product asks people to choose one value from a closed list — a country, a unit, a role — in a box that stands beside its text inputs and is the same box, and it opens a list drawn as its menus are, with the chosen option marked: a surface with its corners, lift and paddings, rows with a text, a second line and a glyph, groups with a title and a divider or a gap between them, each row at rest, hovered, focused, pressed, chosen or disabled. The box has the one box's tokens; the rows around it are the Field's.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: What a select draws that is its own: the list it opens. Its surface, corners, lift, paddings, offset from the box, margin to the window's edge, least and greatest width and greatest height; per density (regular, compact) an option's least height, paddings, gap, glyph and check sizes and a group title's inset; an option's corners and text styles; a group's title, the divider or the gap between groups; the motion of opening and closing and of a row's state change, and a row's opacity in each state; and an option's colors at rest and chosen, in each state. The box is comp.input-box.*.
rules: A select chooses exactly one value from a closed list and holds it as a form value. For actions use a menu; for several values use checkboxes or a list with multiple selection; for a list a person filters by typing use a combobox.
With up to about five options that fit on the screen, radio buttons or tabs show every choice at once and cost one press less; use a select where the options are many or the space is small.

A select is the bare box and its list: it has no label row, no requirement tag, no help and no error text. In a form use the select field, which is a Field around a select; the tokens of those rows are comp.field.*.

The box — container, edges, floating label, the line that shows the chosen value (input), the chevron (trailing-icon, at icon.size), heights and paddings at small, medium and large, and the colors of each look in each state — is comp.input-box.*, shared with the text input, the combobox, the number input and the color input. This group holds only the list.
Every value of the list and of an option equals the menu's (comp.menu.surface.color, …). Change them together in a layer, or a product's lists stop reading as one kind.

The list's parts are list.*, option.*, group-title.*, divider.*, group.gap and status.* (the row after the options that says the source is loading, failed, or gave nothing); an option's colors are each variant's option.* and selected-option.* parts, the same under every variant.
The chosen option is the quiet selection: the selected-option fill with a check at the end of its row. The fill never carries the choice alone.
list.max-height caps a long list, which then scrolls.

option.state-layer.color and selected-option.state-layer.color are the colors the state layers mix into a row. motion.state-duration, motion.state-easing and the four opacity tokens are the rows'; the box has its own in comp.input-box.
compact is for a tool used with a pointer, where rows are many and looked through often; touch always gets rows of the touch target. The density never changes a text style.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never fork the component.

color.$description: The list's surface: the raised sheet a menu and a popover are drawn on.

padding-block.$description: Inset above the first option and below the last.

padding-inline.$description: Inset at the sides of the options. With an option's own padding it puts an option's label under the value the trigger shows.

min-width.$description: The least width of the list where its options and its trigger are narrower than this (a small select in a bar).

max-width.$description: The widest the list grows for its options where its trigger is narrower: an option that needs more wraps. A list is never narrower than its trigger, so a trigger wider than this gives the list its own width. The window limits it further.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides how far a list of choices may grow past a narrow trigger for options with long labels or a second line, before they wrap, so that an open list reads in few lines without covering the form beside it.

max-height.$description: The tallest the list grows before its options scroll: six rows and most of a seventh at the default row height, so that a cut row shows there is more. The room left in the window limits it further.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides how much of a long list of choices — countries, time zones, tokens — it shows at once before the list scrolls, so that an open list does not cover the form it belongs to.

offset.$description: Distance between the trigger and its list.

viewport-margin.$description: How close the list may come to the window's edge.

shape.$description: The corners of an option's row: the list's corner less the inset the rows stand at, so that the two curves keep one distance.

padding-inline.$description: Padding at the sides of an option's row.

padding-block.$description: Padding above and below an option's content.

gap.$description: Distance between an option's glyph, its text and its check.

typescale.$description: The line below an option's label.

size.$description: The box of the check at the end of the chosen option's row, kept in every row so that labels wrap alike.

padding-inline.$description: Inset of a group's heading from the rows' edges.

typescale.$description: The status row's text and the text shown while the select holds no option.

color.$description: The status row's text while nothing is wrong, and the text shown while the select holds no option: secondary to the options.
The status row's text while status is error. The words say what failed; the color says that something did.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product fills some of its selects from a source that takes time or can fail — the projects of an account, the people of a team — and must say, in the list, that it is waiting, that it failed, or that there is nothing to choose; how quiet that line is beside the options is its choice.

gap.$description: The space between two groups while separation is gap.

color.$description: The one hairline, between two groups while separation is divider.

space.$description: Space above and below the divider.

separation.$description: How a group of options is told from what is next to it: divider or gap. Follows the system's choice; a select's separation prop overrides it. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product parts the groups of its selects' lists as it parts the rest, and must be able to set the lists of its forms apart.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: So that a select resolves as the menu does. It restates tanrei.comp.menu.separation: Material's menus part their groups with a line, while its joined buttons and progress indicators use a gap.

state-duration.$description: How long a change of colors and edge widths takes.

feedback-duration.$description: How long a ripple takes to grow over a pressed option.

open-duration.$description: How long the list takes to appear.

close-duration.$description: How long the list takes to go.

stacked.$description: The stacked select. Every part of the trigger holds the value the stacked text input's part of the same name holds; an option holds the menu item's, at rest and chosen.

option.$description: An option's row that is not the chosen one: the menu item's colors at rest. Declared under each variant because the state mechanism values parts per variant; the three hold the same values.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: An item has no fill at rest; the menu's surface shows through.

selected-option.$description: The chosen option's row: the quiet selection's role under its own content color, and the check in the mark color. The default system values the fill as a layer of the row's content color, as it does the menu's checked row (tokens.md, "Rules").

filled.$description: The filled select. Every part of the trigger holds the value the filled text input's part of the same name holds; an option holds the menu item's, at rest and chosen.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: An item has no fill at rest; the menu's surface shows through.

outlined.$description: The outlined select. Every part of the trigger holds the value the outlined text input's part of the same name holds; an option holds the menu item's, at rest and chosen.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: An item has no fill at rest; the menu's surface shows through.
